question: Should Browser CLI `--fields-file` adopt a new 1 MiB hard user-facing limit, and if so what supported upgrade behavior and documentation should accompany it?
rationale: The patch deliberately changes previously unbounded valid input into a runtime error; source-level tests cannot establish whether 1 MiB is the intended product contract for existing automation.

options.title: Approve a documented 1 MiB limit
options.body: Keep the cap after documenting the user-facing limit and adding real CLI proof for both the accepted and rejected paths.

options.title: Choose a different compatibility-safe limit
options.body: Retain bounded reading but set a maintainer-approved threshold that better matches expected Browser form payloads and document it.

options.title: Avoid a new hard limit
options.body: Use a resource-safety approach that does not newly reject existing valid fields files until a formal input-size contract is agreed.

recommendation.title: Approve a documented 1 MiB limit
recommendation.body: Keep the cap after documenting the user-facing limit and adding real CLI proof for both the accepted and rejected paths.
